title: The 8 Levels of Silent Phone Panic
house: A bustling neon-lit metropolis where anthropomorphic fruit and vegetable citizens navigate careers, rent prices, and parental expectations while glowing numbers on their foreheads dictate their social worth.
catchphrase: The number on your forehead never rings.
links: Level 3 Toby mentions a nervous pineapple barista who drops extra-hot espresso on customers.

levels.open_loop: What hidden emergency was my mother actually calling about while my screen flashed red?

gegenspieler.tat: Publicly insults poor Leo in the subway crowd and mocks his forehead number: '1,150 dollars? With so a bankruptcy number I would not even dare to answer my mother.'

levels.name: Leo, 22, Intern
levels.story: The 8 levels of silent phone panic. Level 1. 1,150 dollars? With so a bankruptcy number I would not even dare to answer my mother. Level 1: 1,150 dollars in my bank account and my phone starts vibrating like an angry hornet. I freeze right inside the packed Brooklyn subway car during morning rush hour. My mom's name pops up on the screen with five missed calls already staring at me. I slam my thumb onto the silent mode button so fast my green apple skin nearly scuffs. You cannot afford to ignore your family with a poverty badge like that. My heart hammers against my ribs while commuters stare at my pathetic glowing digits. I keep my head down and stare at the sticky subway floor in pure shame. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Mia, 25, Barista
levels.story: The 8 levels of silent phone panic. Level 2. You let your mother get pushed away while you throw a half-baked macchiato at me? No wonder with 2,400 dollars tip poverty. Level 2: 2,400 dollars monthly tip jar income and my phone buzzes against the espresso machine. My mother's face flashes on the screen while steam hisses loudly from the milk wand. I swipe it to silent mode instantly so my boss doesn't dock my hourly wage. Answer your mother right now instead of ruining my macchiato order. My hands shake so badly I spill oat milk all over the stainless steel drip tray. She points at my forehead number and rolls her eyes at the cafe patrons watching us. I bite my lip to stop the hot tears stinging behind my eyelids right there. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Marcus, 31, Accountant
levels.story: The 8 levels of silent phone panic. Level 3. Six grand salary and trembling like a schoolboy before dad? The shareholders are laughing at your fear. Level 3: 6,400 dollars a month in corporate salary and my desk phone starts blaring right during the tax audit meeting. My father's name lights up the caller ID with a red warning badge. I hit the mute button so fast my tailored cufflink snaps against the mahogany table. You look terrified of your parents for someone making six grand. The auditors stare at my forehead numbers like I am a walking spreadsheet error. I adjust my collar to hide the sweat pooling beneath my dragonfruit skin tone. They think I have it all figured out, but my family demands perfection every single hour. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Clara, 38, Architect
levels.story: The 8 levels of silent phone panic. Level 4. With almost ten thousand dollars honorarium still a trauma from your parents' house? You are embarrassing for this floor. Level 4: 9,800 dollars net consulting fee per month and my cell phone starts howling like a siren during a design pitch. My mother's emergency number flashes across the screen in bold crimson letters. I slam the phone face down onto the architectural blueprint table so fast my ink pen shatters. You are too old to be shaking over a family call when your number is nearly ten grand. The junior draftsmen stare at my forehead display, whispering among themselves about my sudden panic. My pristine velvet coat feels like a straitjacket under their judging gazes. I built this firm from scratch, yet one ring from home reduces me to a terrified child. You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.story: The 8 levels of silent phone panic. Level 6. Twenty-two thousand rent and whining like a tenant before eviction? Pitiful. My rough coconut shell skin breaks out in cold sweat beneath the crystal chandeliers. I own half of Manhattan, but my family's shadow still controls every breath I take. You'll see that in Level 7.

levels.name: Victoria, 50, Empire Founder
levels.story: The 8 levels of silent phone panic. Level 8. Level 8: 50,000 plus dollars daily empire revenue and every single phone in the penthouse starts ringing simultaneously. The entire room falls dead silent as hundreds of screens flash with my own childhood phone number. I look down at my glowing infinity badge and realize the number on our foreheads was never about money. You have the empire, but you are just as scared as all of us. The universal panic that binds every fruit and vegetable citizen connects us all in the end. I take a deep breath, touch my glowing display, and finally press accept on the call that started it all. The number on your forehead never rings, but the truth finally speaks. Which series should we explore next?
